visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 correctly shows the projectile arc, launch angle/components, flight time, and range value in the right locations, while Lesson 1’s Desmos setup remains visually broken with warning icons, missing/undefined angle input, no actual trajectory plotted, and no readable correct range displayed.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a well-formed, wired fill-in gate after act_introduction with a real prompt, accepted answer, hint, and remediation path, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning checkpoints.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 is clearly paced and natural with spoken math handled well, while Lesson 1 has awkward repetition, less polished phrasing, and a defective irrelevant ending fragment about a golfer.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed visual cues that generally correspond to the narrated references despite a few early offsets, whereas Lesson 1 has no cue/timing data at all while describing visual actions like showing the arc and clicking the endpoint, so its sync is unsupported and likely worse.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is mathematically correct and builds understanding through velocity decomposition, vertical time-of-flight, and constant horizontal motion, whereas Lesson 1 gives the right numerical range but mostly describes plotting/clicking in Desmos without explaining the equations or reasoning and even ends with an irrelevant fragment.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a cleaner, more visually consistent dark layout with fewer distracting overlays, while Lesson 1 is heavily cluttered by platform UI elements, chat mascot, subtitles, Desmos controls, warning icons, and a final modal that make the presentation feel messy despite some large readable text.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents prefer Lesson 2, mostly with very high confidence. Lesson 2 is visually accurate with a correct projectile arc and labels, has functioning interactivity, clearer narration, better timed visual synchronization, stronger conceptual explanation of projectile motion, and a more polished presentation. Lesson 1 suffers from broken or missing visual elements, no functioning checkpoints, weaker narration, unsupported sync, shallow conceptual explanation, cluttered UI, and irrelevant ending content.
